questions.question: Of which among the following is ‘parsec’ a unit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Length**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parsec** is a unit of **length** used in astronomy to measure large distances to objects outside our Solar System.
 
• One parsec is approximately equal to **3.26 light-years**, or about **3.086 × 10¹⁶ meters**.
 
• The term "parsec" originates from the method of measurement using the concept of **parallax**, where the angle of parallax is one arcsecond (1/3600 of a degree).
 
• It is commonly used to express distances to stars, galaxies, and other celestial objects.
 
• Parsec is preferred in astronomy over other units like kilometers or miles due to its convenience in representing extremely vast distances. *Hence, 'Length' is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Units of Measurement in Astronomy:**

 
 
• **Light-year:** A unit of distance representing the distance light travels in one year, approximately **9.46 × 10¹² kilometers**.
 
• **Astronomical Unit (AU):** Represents the average distance between the Earth and the Sun, about **149.6 million kilometers**.
 
• **Kiloparsec (kpc):** A larger unit used to measure distances within galaxies, equivalent to **1000 parsecs**.
 
• **Megaparsec (Mpc):** Used for intergalactic distances, equivalent to **1 million parsecs**.
 
 
 
• **What is Parallax?**
 
 
• **Parallax** is the apparent shift in the position of an object when viewed from two different vantage points.
 
• In astronomy, it is used to measure the distance to nearby stars by observing their position changes relative to distant background stars.
 
• The distance measured is inversely proportional to the angle of parallax, expressed in arcseconds.
 
 
 
• **Why Parsecs are Important?**
 
 
• Parsecs simplify the calculation and representation of distances in the vast expanse of space.
 
• They are vital in understanding the scale of the universe and the position of celestial objects.
 
• Most astronomical distances, such as those in star catalogs, are listed in parsecs for ease of scientific calculations.

questions.question: The Indian Constitution provides _____ types of funds to the Central Government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Constitution** provides **three types of funds** to the Central Government, ensuring proper financial management and accountability.
 
• These funds are the **Consolidated Fund of India**, the **Contingency Fund of India**, and the **Public Account of India**.
 
• The **Consolidated Fund of India** (Article 266) is the most important fund and includes all revenues received by the government, loans raised, and money received in repayment of loans.
 
• The **Contingency Fund of India** (Article 267) is used for urgent or unforeseen expenditures and requires parliamentary approval for replenishment.
 
• The **Public Account of India** consists of funds held by the government in trust, such as provident funds, small savings, and other deposits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Consolidated Fund of India:**

 
 
• All revenues generated through direct and indirect taxes, custom duties, and other income sources are credited to this fund.
 
• It also includes money borrowed by the government and repayment of loans.
 
• Expenditures from this fund require parliamentary approval.
 
• Examples include spending on defense, infrastructure, and salaries of government employees.
 
 
 
• **Contingency Fund of India:**
 
 
• Established under Article 267 of the Constitution, it is used for emergencies or unforeseen expenditures.
 
• It is maintained by the Finance Ministry and replenished with parliamentary approval.
 
• The fund has a fixed corpus, currently at **Rs. 500 crore**, which can be increased if needed.
 
 
 
• **Public Account of India:**
 
 
• It includes funds held in trust by the government, such as provident funds, small savings schemes, and other deposits.
 
• These funds do not belong to the government but are managed by it for specific purposes.
 
• Examples include disbursement of pensions, scholarships, and small savings withdrawals.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Parliamentary approval is mandatory for expenditure from the Consolidated Fund and Contingency Fund.
 
• Public Account funds are not subject to parliamentary approval, as they are held in trust.
 
• These funds are vital for maintaining fiscal discipline and ensuring transparency in public finances.

questions.question: Urine produced in the kidneys passes through the ureters to the bladder where it is stored.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ureter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **ureters** are a pair of thin muscular tubes that connect the kidneys to the bladder. They transport urine produced in the kidneys to the bladder for storage. *This statement is correct.*
 
• The **urethra**, in contrast, is the tube through which urine exits the bladder and is expelled from the body. It is not involved in urine transport from the kidneys. *Hence, option 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The **aorta** is the largest artery in the human body, responsible for transporting oxygenated blood from the heart to various parts of the body. It is unrelated to the urinary system. *Hence, option 3 is incorrect.*
 
• The **vena cava** is a major vein that carries deoxygenated blood back to the heart. It is also unrelated to the process of urine transport. *Hence, option 4 is incorrect.*
 
• Urine is stored in the bladder until it is expelled from the body through the urethra. The process of urine formation and transport involves the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra. *Statement in the question is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ureter:**

 
 
• The ureters are narrow tubes, approximately **10-12 inches long**, that transport urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
 
• They are lined with smooth muscle tissue that contracts rhythmically in a process known as **peristalsis** to move urine effectively.
 
• The upper end of the ureters is connected to the renal pelvis of the kidneys, while the lower end opens into the bladder.
 
• Blockages or infections in the ureters can lead to medical conditions such as **hydronephrosis** or urinary tract infections.
 
 
 
• **Urethra:**
 
 
• The urethra is the final part of the urinary system through which urine is expelled from the bladder during urination.
 
• In males, the urethra is longer and also serves as a passage for semen during ejaculation. In females, it is shorter and serves only the urinary function.
 
 
 
• **Aorta:**
 
 
• The aorta is the main artery that arises from the heart and carries oxygen-rich blood to the body.
 
• It has no role in the urinary system but is vital for the circulatory system.
 
 
 
• **Vena Cava:**
 
 
• The vena cava includes two main veins: the **superior vena cava** and the **inferior vena cava**, which return deoxygenated blood to the heart.
 
• Like the aorta, it is not involved in the urinary process but is critical for circulation.
 
 
 
• **Urinary System Functions:**
 
 
• The urinary system consists of the kidneys, ureters, bladder, and urethra, and its primary function is to remove waste and excess substances from the blood.
 
• The kidneys filter the blood to produce urine, which travels through the ureters to the bladder and then exits the body via the urethra.
 
• This system helps maintain **fluid balance**, **electrolyte levels**, and **blood pressure regulation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Urine Formation:**

 
 
• The kidneys filter approximately **50 gallons of blood** daily to produce **1-2 liters of urine.**
 
• Urine formation involves three processes: **glomerular filtration**, **tubular reabsorption**, and **tubular secretion**.
 
 
 
• **Medical Issues:**
 
 
• Common disorders include **kidney stones**, **urinary tract infections**, and **bladder dysfunction.**
 
• Maintaining hydration is key for preventing issues related to urine transport and kidney health.

questions.question: The evaporation of water molecules in the form of water vapour from the stomata on leaves is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**transpiration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transpiration** is the process by which **water evaporates** from the surface of leaves, primarily through **stomata**.
 
• It is a crucial physiological process in plants as it helps in **maintaining water balance** and facilitates the uptake of nutrients from the soil.
 
• Transpiration also plays a significant role in the **cooling mechanism** of plants by releasing water vapor.
 
• Approximately **90% of the water absorbed** by plants is lost through transpiration, while the remaining water is utilized for growth and metabolic activities.
 
• Factors such as **temperature, humidity, wind speed, light intensity,** and the number of stomata influence the rate of transpiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Stomata:**

 
 
• Stomata are tiny openings on the surfaces of leaves, stems, and other plant organs.
 
• They are primarily responsible for facilitating **gas exchange** and **water vapor loss** during transpiration.
 
• Guard cells regulate the opening and closing of stomata based on environmental conditions such as light and humidity.
 
 
 
• **Respiration:**
 
 
• Respiration refers to the metabolic process by which organisms convert **glucose into energy** in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate).
 
• This process occurs in all living cells, including plant cells, but it is different from transpiration.
 
 
 
• **Perspiration:**
 
 
• Perspiration is the process of releasing sweat from sweat glands in animals and humans to regulate body temperature.
 
• It is unrelated to transpiration, which occurs in plants.
 
 
 
• **Transcription:**
 
 
• Transcription is a biological process where genetic information from DNA is transcribed into RNA.
 
• It is a molecular mechanism and does not involve the evaporation of water, unlike transpiration.
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
• **Evaporation vs Transpiration:** While evaporation refers to the loss of water from any surface, transpiration specifically refers to the loss of water vapor from plants.
 
• Transpiration contributes to the **water cycle** by returning water to the atmosphere.
 
• Plants like **cacti** have adaptations to minimize transpiration, such as reduced leaf surface area and thick cuticles.

questions.question: Which of the following mountain ranges are located in South America?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Andes**: The Andes mountain range is located in **South America** and is the world's longest continental mountain range. It stretches over seven countries: **Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, and Argentina**.
 
• The Andes form the backbone of South America and extend for about **7,000 km** along the continent's western coast.
 
• They feature diverse landscapes including high plateaus, volcanic peaks, and deep valleys. The Andes are home to the **Atacama Desert**, one of the driest places on Earth.
 
• The Andes are known for their significant cultural history, as they were central to ancient civilizations like the **Incas**. They are also important for modern-day mining, agriculture, and tourism.
 
• **Hence, the correct answer is Andes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alps:**

 
 
• The Alps are located in **Europe**, spanning countries like France, Italy, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, and Slovenia.
 
• They are known for their breathtaking landscapes, skiing resorts, and glacial features.
 
• The Alps are shorter than the Andes, stretching for about **1,200 km**.
 
 
 
• **Great Dividing Range:**
 
 
• The Great Dividing Range is the most prominent mountain range in **Australia**.
 
• It runs parallel to the eastern coast of Australia and spans about **3,500 km**.
 
• It is characterized by ancient landforms, forests, and biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Rocky Mountains:**
 
 
• The Rocky Mountains are located in **North America**, stretching across the United States and Canada.
 
• They span approximately **4,800 km** and are known for their rugged terrain and natural beauty.
 
• The Rockies are home to several national parks, including Yellowstone and Glacier National Park.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Andes:**
 
 
• The Andes are rich in **natural resources** such as copper, silver, and gold, making them an important mining region.
 
• The mountain range has a diverse ecosystem that supports unique wildlife and plant species.
 
• The Andes are also vital for agriculture, particularly for crops like potatoes and quinoa.
 
• The range plays a crucial role in the cultural and historical identity of South America.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Andes' Geological Features:**

 
 
• The Andes are largely formed by the subduction of the **Nazca Plate** beneath the South American Plate.
 
• They contain several active volcanoes, such as **Mount Cotopaxi** and **Mount Ojos del Salado**.
 
• The Andes also house **Lake Titicaca**, the highest navigable lake in the world.
 
 
 
• **Climate Zones:**
 
 
• The Andes exhibit diverse climate zones, ranging from tropical forests in the north to glaciers in the south.
 
• They play a significant role in influencing the weather patterns across South America.

questions.question: Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands have been named as the ‘______’ by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Mission Blue, an organisation involved in the study of oceans.

The correct answer is __**Hope Spot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• A **Hope Spot** is a special place that is critical to the health of the ocean. These areas are scientifically identified as being vital for the marine ecosystem and biodiversity conservation.
 
• The recognition highlights these islands' importance in promoting **marine conservation** and protecting diverse marine species, coral reefs, and ecosystems.
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep Islands are known for their rich **marine biodiversity**, including vibrant coral reefs, mangroves, seagrass beds, and numerous marine species.
 
• This designation aims to raise awareness about the need to preserve these ecosystems and encourages sustainable practices in the region to protect them from threats like **climate change**, **pollution**, and **overfishing**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN):**

 
 
• The **IUCN** is a global organization established in **1948** that works to conserve nature and promote sustainable use of natural resources.
 
• It is responsible for the **Red List of Threatened Species**, which assesses the conservation status of species worldwide.
 
• The IUCN collaborates with governments, NGOs, scientists, and local communities to address environmental challenges.
 
 
 
• **Mission Blue:**
 
 
• **Mission Blue** is an initiative launched by marine biologist **Dr. Sylvia Earle** to promote ocean conservation and identify Hope Spots around the globe.
 
• The organization aims to inspire public support for marine protected areas and sustainable ocean practices.
 
• Mission Blue has identified over **100 Hope Spots** worldwide, focusing on areas critical for marine ecosystem health.
 
 
 
• **Coral Reefs in Andaman, Nicobar, and Lakshadweep:**
 
 
• The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** are home to over **500 species** of coral and are among the most biodiverse marine ecosystems in the world.
 
• The **Lakshadweep Islands** also have extensive coral reefs, which act as natural barriers against storms and erosion.
 
• These reefs are vital for supporting marine life, including fish, sea turtles, and crustaceans.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Hope Spots:**
 
 
• Hope Spots serve as symbols of hope for the future of marine conservation and encourage global efforts to restore ocean health.
 
• They play a key role in maintaining marine biodiversity, regulating the global climate, and supporting livelihoods of coastal communities.
 
• Recognition as a Hope Spot brings international attention and often leads to increased funding and conservation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Threats to Marine Ecosystems:**
 
 
• Marine ecosystems face various threats, including **climate change**, which leads to coral bleaching and rising sea levels.
 
• Other threats include **overfishing**, **marine pollution** (plastic waste, oil spills), and destruction of habitats due to coastal development.
 
• Conservation initiatives like designating Hope Spots aim to mitigate these threats and promote sustainable practices.

questions.question: In September 2020, the Railway Protection Force of India disrupted the operation of illegal software called ______ used for cornering confirmed railway reservation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Real Mango**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **September 2020**, the **Railway Protection Force (RPF)** of India disrupted the operation of illegal software called **Real Mango** that was used for cornering confirmed railway reservations.
 
• **Real Mango** was an unauthorized software designed to bypass the railway reservation system and secure confirmed tickets fraudulently by manipulating the booking process.
 
• The software enabled agents to book tickets at a rapid pace, exploiting the **tatkal ticket system** and depriving genuine passengers of their chance to secure bookings.
 
• The **Railway Protection Force** conducted raids across different locations in India, resulting in the arrest of individuals involved in the operation of this illegal software.
 
• The disruption of the **Real Mango** software by RPF was aimed at curbing the malpractice and ensuring a fair ticketing system for passengers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Railway Protection Force (RPF):**

 
 
• The **Railway Protection Force** is a security force under the Ministry of Railways, tasked with protecting railway passengers, property, and infrastructure.
 
• Established under the **Railways Act, 1989**, the RPF has the authority to investigate crimes related to railway operations.
 
• RPF plays a crucial role in curbing cyber fraud and illegal practices in railway bookings.
 
 
 
• **Tatkal Ticket System:**
 
 
• The **tatkal ticket system** is a special quota in Indian Railways introduced to facilitate last-minute bookings for urgent travel requirements.
 
• Tickets under this system are booked on a first-come, first-serve basis, with a specific window for reservations opening 24 hours before the train's departure.
 
• Due to high demand, tatkal tickets are susceptible to misuse, leading to the development of illegal software like **Real Mango**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Illegal Software:**
 
 
• Illegal software like **Real Mango** compromises the integrity of the railway reservation system and causes inconvenience to genuine passengers.
 
• Such software is often operated by unauthorized agents who exploit loopholes in the system for financial gain.
 
 
 
• **Steps Taken by Indian Railways:**
 
 
• Indian Railways has implemented robust measures to prevent misuse of the reservation system, including advanced cybersecurity protocols.
 
• Regular monitoring and audits of the reservation process are conducted to detect and eliminate fraudulent activities.
 
 
 
• **Other Illegal Booking Software:**
 
 
• In addition to **Real Mango**, other illegal booking software like **Rare Mango** and **Black TS** have been identified and disrupted by authorities in the past.
 
• These software tools exploit the reservation system and are typically operated by organized networks.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Consequences:**

 
 
• Operating illegal software like **Real Mango** is a punishable offense under the **Railways Act, 1989**.
 
• Individuals involved in such activities face legal action, including imprisonment and fines.
 
 
 
• **Public Awareness:**
 
 
• Indian Railways regularly conducts awareness campaigns to educate passengers about the risks associated with illegal booking practices.
 
• Passengers are advised to use only authorized platforms for ticket bookings.

__
 
• The term **Lame-duck session** refers to the last session of the outgoing Lok Sabha after a new Lok Sabha has been elected.
 
• It is called so because the members of the outgoing Lok Sabha are no longer politically significant since a new Lok Sabha will soon take over.
 
• During this session, the members of the outgoing House do not have the authority to make major decisions or enact any significant policies.
 
• The term "lame-duck" is often used in a broader political context to denote a situation where the authority of a governing body or an official is diminished due to the imminent transfer of power.
 
• Such sessions are rare and may occur when the timing of elections and parliamentary sessions overlap.

• As per Article 100 of the Constitution of India, the quorum for a meeting of either House is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House.
 
 
 
• **Sine Die:**
 
 
• The term "adjournment sine die" means adjourning a session of Parliament for an indefinite period without specifying the date for the next meeting.
 
• This usually happens when the agenda of the session is completed or if the House faces unavoidable circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Pro Tem Speaker:**
 
 
• A Pro Tem Speaker is appointed temporarily to conduct the first meeting of a newly elected Lok Sabha or the state legislative assembly.
 
• The primary duty of the Pro Tem Speaker is to oversee the swearing-in of new members and the election of the regular Speaker.
 
 
 
• **Lame-duck Sessions in Other Countries:**

questions.question: The summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere occurs in the month of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**June**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **summer solstice** in the **Northern Hemisphere** occurs every year around **June 21st**. This marks the longest day of the year in terms of daylight hours.
 
• It happens when the **Earth's axial tilt** is closest to the Sun, with the North Pole tilted directly toward it. This results in the Sun appearing at its **highest point in the sky** for observers in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
• During the summer solstice, regions in the Northern Hemisphere experience the maximum amount of **sunlight**, while locations above the Arctic Circle witness **24 hours of daylight**, commonly known as the "Midnight Sun."
 
• The occurrence of solstices (both summer and winter) is due to the Earth's **23.5-degree axial tilt** relative to its orbit around the Sun. This tilt causes variations in sunlight distribution across the planet.
 
• This event is significant in various cultures and is often celebrated through **festivals**, rituals, and traditions, such as the well-known **Stonehenge gatherings in England**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **What is a Solstice?**

 
 
• The term **solstice** is derived from the Latin words "sol" (Sun) and "sistere" (to stand still). It refers to the time when the Sun appears to pause at its northernmost or southernmost position before reversing direction.
 
• The two types of solstices are the **summer solstice** (around June 21) and the **winter solstice** (around December 21).
 
 
 
• **Seasonal Changes Due to Earth's Tilt:**
 
 
• The Earth's axial tilt of **23.5 degrees** is the primary reason for the changing seasons. It affects how sunlight is distributed across the planet throughout the year.
 
• During the summer solstice, the **Northern Hemisphere** is tilted toward the Sun, resulting in longer days and shorter nights.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Summer Solstice:**
 
 
• It has cultural and historical importance in many parts of the world. For example, **Stonehenge** in England aligns with the sunrise on the summer solstice, making it a site of annual gatherings.
 
• In some countries, festivals such as **Midsummer** in Scandinavia and **Inti Raymi** in Peru are held to honor the solstice.
 
 
 
• **Differences Between the Hemispheres:**
 
 
• While the Northern Hemisphere experiences summer solstice in **June**, the Southern Hemisphere witnesses its winter solstice at the same time.
 
• Similarly, the Southern Hemisphere's summer solstice occurs in **December**, coinciding with the Northern Hemisphere's winter solstice.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The summer solstice marks the start of **astronomical summer**, as opposed to meteorological summer which begins on June 1st.
 
• The length of daylight varies by location. For instance, places near the equator experience minimal variation in day length, while higher latitudes see significant differences.
 
• The Sun appears to "stand still" at its zenith during the solstice, which is why the day is named so.

questions.question: According to Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, the long-billed vulture, commonly known as the Indian vulture, is a part of ______ as of August, 2020.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Schedule I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **long-billed vulture**, commonly known as the **Indian vulture**, is listed under **Schedule I** of the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972** as of August 2020.
 
• Schedule I provides the **highest level of protection** to species, making it illegal to hunt or trade them. Violations can result in severe penalties, including imprisonment and fines.
 
• The inclusion of the Indian vulture in Schedule I highlights its **critically endangered status** and the urgent need for its conservation.
 
• Indian vultures have faced severe population declines in recent decades, primarily due to the use of the veterinary drug **diclofenac**, which is toxic to vultures when they consume carcasses of treated livestock.
 
• The government and various non-governmental organizations have initiated **vulture conservation programs**, including breeding programs and the promotion of safer alternatives to diclofenac.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972:**

 
 
• This act was enacted by the **Indian government** to protect the country's wildlife and their habitats.
 
• The act classifies species into different schedules, providing varying degrees of protection. Schedule I offers the **highest level of protection**, followed by Schedules II, III, IV, and V.
 
• Hunting or trading species listed under Schedule I is **strictly prohibited**, with violations subject to stringent penalties.
 
 
 
• **Indian Vulture:**
 
 
• The Indian vulture (*Gyps indicus*) is a medium-sized vulture found in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the ecosystem by **disposing of animal carcasses**, preventing the spread of diseases.
 
• Its population has declined by over **99%** since the early 1990s, primarily due to **diclofenac poisoning**.
 
 
 
• **Diclofenac and its Impact:**
 
 
• Diclofenac is a **non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID)** used to treat livestock.
 
• Vultures feeding on carcasses of animals treated with diclofenac suffer from **kidney failure**, leading to their death.
 
• India banned the veterinary use of diclofenac in **2006**, but illegal use still persists.
 
 
 
• **Vulture Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• The Indian government, along with organizations like the **Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS)**, has established **vulture breeding centers** to boost their population.
 
• Programs promoting the use of alternative drugs like **meloxicam**, which are safe for vultures, have been implemented.
 
• International initiatives like the **Save Asia’s Vultures from Extinction (SAVE)** program are also working towards the conservation of vultures.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **long-billed vulture** is classified as **Critically Endangered** by the **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)**.
 
• Other species of vultures, such as the slender-billed vulture (*Gyps tenuirostris*) and white-rumped vulture (*Gyps bengalensis*), are also listed as Critically Endangered under IUCN.
 
• Vultures are considered a **keystone species** in the ecosystem, indicating the health of the environment and biodiversity.

• The mosque was built by **Qutub-ud-Din Aibak**, the founder of the **Delhi Sultanate**, during his reign after defeating **Prithviraj Chauhan** in the second battle of Tarain.

questions.question: The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act was passed in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act was passed in 1856**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hindu Widow Remarriage Act** was enacted in the year **1856** during British rule in India.
 
• This act was introduced to **remove societal restrictions** on the remarriage of Hindu widows, a practice that was largely opposed by traditional Hindu society.
 
• The act was championed by **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**, a renowned social reformer, who played a pivotal role in advocating for widow remarriage and reforming Hindu society.
 
• The law allowed widows to remarry while safeguarding their rights, such as the forfeiture of property inherited from their deceased husbands.
 
• The act was a significant step toward improving the **socio-economic conditions** of widows and promoting gender equality during the 19th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of the Hindu Widow Remarriage Act:**

 
 
• Prior to the enactment of the act, Hindu widows were subject to severe restrictions, including **social isolation**, prohibition from wearing colorful clothing, and denial of remarriage.
 
• The movement for widow remarriage was led by **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**, who strongly opposed these oppressive practices and worked tirelessly to bring reforms.
 
• He cited **ancient Hindu scriptures** to argue that widow remarriage was permissible and should be encouraged.
 
 
 
• **Provisions of the Act:**
 
 
• The act legalized the remarriage of Hindu widows, giving them a chance to lead a dignified life.
 
• It ensured that a widow who remarried would lose her claim to any property inherited from her first husband. This provision aimed to protect the interests of the deceased husband's family.
 
 
 
• **Role of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar:**
 
 
• Vidyasagar is considered a key figure behind this legislation. His efforts included writing extensively on the subject and lobbying the British government for reform.
 
• He faced resistance from orthodox Hindu communities but remained steadfast in his advocacy for widow rights.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Act:**
 
 
• The act marked a turning point in Indian society, initiating the process of social reform for women.
 
• It challenged the traditional norms and paved the way for further reforms in women's rights and gender equality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Social Reform Movements:**

 
 
• The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act was part of a series of social reform movements during the 19th century aimed at improving the condition of women in India.
 
• Other reforms included the abolition of **sati** (widow burning) and the introduction of women's education.
 
 
 
• **Legal Significance:**
 
 
• This act was one of the earliest legislations passed by the British government in India to address social issues.
 
• It set a precedent for the government to intervene in religious and cultural practices to promote social justice.
 
 
 
• **Resistance and Challenges:**
 
 
• The act faced strong opposition from conservative sections of society who believed it went against traditional Hindu practices.
 
• Despite the opposition, it was a critical step toward gender equality and social progress.

questions.question: Which of the following books is written by E.M. Forster?

The correct answer is __**A Passage to India**__.

__
 
• **E.M. Forster** is the renowned author of **"A Passage to India."** This novel is considered one of his masterpieces and was published in **1924**.
 
• The novel explores themes such as **colonialism, friendship, and cultural conflict**, set in the backdrop of the **British colonial rule in India.**
 
• **"A Passage to India"** examines the complex relationships between the British colonizers and the native Indians, focusing on the interactions between Dr. Aziz, an Indian Muslim, and two British characters, Cyril Fielding and Adela Quested.
 
• This work is highly acclaimed for its portrayal of the **social and political dynamics** of India during the colonial period and is still widely studied for its literary and historical significance.
 
• None of the other options listed, including **"The Hungry Tide," "Train to Pakistan,"** or **"The Other Side of Silence,"** are written by E.M. Forster.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Hungry Tide:**

 
 
• This book was written by **Amitav Ghosh** and published in **2004.**
 
• It is set in the **Sundarbans region of India** and deals with themes of environmental conservation, human displacement, and the clash of cultures.
 
 
 
• **Train to Pakistan:**
 
 
• Authored by **Khushwant Singh**, this novel was published in **1956**.
 
• It provides a vivid depiction of the **Partition of India in 1947** and its impact on individuals and communities.
 
 
 
• **The Other Side of Silence:**
 
 
• Written by **Urvashi Butalia**, this is a non-fiction book published in **1998**.
 
• It delves into the **oral histories** of survivors of the Partition of India, focusing on personal narratives and the silenced voices of women.
 
 
 
• **About E.M. Forster:**
 
 
• **Edward Morgan Forster** (1879–1970) was a British author best known for his novels that explore human relationships and social conventions.
 
• His other notable works include **"Howard’s End"** (1910) and **"A Room with a View"** (1908).
 
• Forster’s writing often reflects themes of **class struggles, colonialism, and personal growth.**

questions.question: The word ‘UNCITRAL’ stands for _________.

options.text: United National Commission on International Trade Law
United National Committee on International Trade Law
United Nations Committee on International Trade Law
United Nations Commission on International Trade Law

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Nations Commission on International Trade Law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The acronym **UNCITRAL** stands for the **United Nations Commission on International Trade Law**. It is a subsidiary body of the United Nations General Assembly.
 
• UNCITRAL was established by the **United Nations General Assembly** in **1966** to promote the progressive harmonization and unification of international trade law.
 
• The organization plays a crucial role in developing global legal frameworks for international trade, ensuring that businesses across borders operate under consistent and fair legal standards.
 
• UNCITRAL’s work includes the drafting of conventions, model laws, and legal guides in areas such as **arbitration, electronic commerce, international payments, insolvency law, and trade finance**.
 
• It consists of **60 member states**, elected by the General Assembly, representing different geographic regions, and ensures that its work reflects diverse legal traditions and economic systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• UNCITRAL was established in **1966** by the **United Nations General Assembly** to address the disparities in national trade laws that hinder international trade.
 
• The first session of UNCITRAL was held in **1968** in **New York**.
 
• Its mandate focuses on creating modern, fair, and harmonized rules for international business transactions.
 
 
 
• **Key Legal Instruments:**
 
 
• UNCITRAL has developed several important legal instruments, including the **United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods (CISG)** and the **Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration**.
 
• These instruments are widely used and have been adopted by numerous countries worldwide to standardize trade practices.
 
 
 
• **Functions of UNCITRAL:**
 
 
• UNCITRAL drafts and promotes the adoption of international conventions and model laws.
 
• It provides technical assistance to states with law reform projects and organizes seminars to improve the understanding and uniformity of international trade law.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Representation:**
 
 
• UNCITRAL’s membership is designed to ensure a balanced representation of different geographic regions and legal traditions.
 
• The **60 member states** are elected by the United Nations General Assembly for six-year terms.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• UNCITRAL’s work is critical in reducing legal barriers and uncertainties in international trade, fostering global economic growth.
 
• It has also contributed significantly to the development of legal frameworks for emerging areas like **electronic commerce** and **cross-border insolvency**.

questions.question: The Muslim League fixed ______ 1946 as the 'Direct Action Day'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aug 16 1946**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Muslim League** declared **August 16, 1946**, as 'Direct Action Day' to demand a separate nation for Muslims, leading to the creation of Pakistan.
 
• **Direct Action Day** was marked by widespread communal riots, especially in **Kolkata (then Calcutta)**, which resulted in loss of lives and property.
 
• The decision to observe Direct Action Day was taken after the rejection of the **Cabinet Mission Plan**, which proposed a united India with autonomy for provinces.
 
• The Muslim League, led by **Mohammad Ali Jinnah**, aimed to showcase the solidarity and strength of the Muslim community in demanding a separate homeland.
 
• On this day, the League organized a strike and demonstrations to emphasize their goal, resulting in the infamous **Calcutta Killings**, which continued for several days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of Direct Action Day:**

 
 
• The **Cabinet Mission Plan** proposed a federal structure for India but was rejected by the Muslim League due to lack of provisions for a separate Pakistan.
 
• The Muslim League decided to intensify its demand for Pakistan, leading to the announcement of Direct Action Day.
 
 
 
• **Calcutta Killings:**
 
 
• The communal violence in Kolkata on **August 16, 1946**, resulted in the deaths of thousands and further deepened the division between Hindus and Muslims.
 
• The riots were fueled by political tensions and heightened communal sentiments following the League's declaration.
 
 
 
• **Role of Mohammad Ali Jinnah:**
 
 
• **Mohammad Ali Jinnah**, leader of the Muslim League, played a pivotal role in advocating for Pakistan and calling for Direct Action Day.
 
• Jinnah’s speeches and actions during this period emphasized the idea of a separate nation for Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Direct Action Day:**
 
 
• The violence and unrest highlighted the deep divisions between religious communities in India.
 
• It paved the way for the eventual partition of India in **1947**, with the creation of India and Pakistan as separate nations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cabinet Mission Plan:**

 
 
• Proposed by British officials in **1946**, the plan aimed to preserve the unity of India while granting autonomy to provinces.
 
• It was rejected by the Muslim League, which demanded a separate nation for Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Partition of India:**
 
 
• The communal tensions and political disagreements culminated in the partition of India on **August 15, 1947**.
 
• India and Pakistan were created as independent nations, with Pakistan designated as a homeland for Muslims.

__
 
• The term "**Thalinomics - the economics of a plate of food in India**" was introduced in the **Economic Survey 2019-20**, prepared by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.
 
• **Thalinomics** aimed to quantify what a common Indian spends on a plate of food (a "thali") and how food affordability has changed over the years.
 
• The analysis in Thalinomics was based on data collected for both **vegetarian and non-vegetarian thalis** across India between **2006-07 and 2019-20**.
 
• The Economic Survey highlighted that due to government policies and interventions, the affordability of thalis had improved significantly, particularly for low-income groups.
 
• This concept provided insights into the impact of inflation, agricultural policies, and supply chain management on food prices and overall economic well-being.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Economic Survey:**

 
 
• The **Economic Survey** is an annual report released by the **Ministry of Finance** before the Union Budget. It assesses the state of the Indian economy over the past financial year.
 
• It provides critical insights into **growth, inflation, employment, fiscal deficit, and economic trends** that help policymakers, economists, and stakeholders.
 
 
 
• **Affordability of Thalis:**
 
 
• According to the Economic Survey 2019-20, the affordability of vegetarian thalis improved by **29%** and non-vegetarian thalis by **20%** during 2006-07 to 2019-20.
 
• This improvement was attributed to **reduced prices of essential food items** such as cereals and pulses, supported by government schemes like **PM-KISAN** and **Price Stabilization Fund**.
 
 
 
• **Government Schemes Supporting Food Affordability:**
 
 
• **PM-KISAN:** Provides income support to farmers by depositing **₹6,000 annually** in their bank accounts.
 
• **National Food Security Act (NFSA):** Ensures subsidized food grains to more than **800 million beneficiaries**.
 
• **Price Stabilization Fund:** Helps stabilize food prices by creating a buffer stock of essential commodities.
 
 
 
• **Economic Survey Themes:**
 
 
• The Economic Survey often includes innovative concepts like **Thalinomics** to simplify economic data for the public.
 
• Other themes in Economic Surveys include **India's demographic dividend**, **Ease of Doing Business**, and **climate change impacts**.

• **Thali Composition:**

 
 
• A vegetarian thali typically includes **rice or rotis, lentils, vegetables, and curd**.
 
• A non-vegetarian thali includes **meat or fish along with other components.**
 
 
 
• **Use of CPI Data:**
 
 
• The affordability analysis in Thalinomics was derived from **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** data.
 
• CPI measures changes in the price levels of goods and services consumed by households.
 
 
 
• **Policy Impact:**
 
 
• The concept of Thalinomics highlighted the **effectiveness** of government schemes in improving living standards.
 
• It emphasized the importance of **agricultural reforms**, public distribution systems, and price regulation.

• During the **first meeting of the National Ganga Council** in **Kanpur on December 14, 2019**, Prime Minister **Shri Narendra Modi** proposed the concept of **Arth Ganga**.
 
• The initiative aims to **energize economic activities** along the banks of the **Ganga River** by integrating the river's ecosystem with socio-economic development.
 
• The **Arth Ganga** model focuses on promoting **sustainable livelihood opportunities** such as organic farming, eco-tourism, and local crafts for communities living along the river.
 
• The program supports the **Namami Gange initiative** by linking river rejuvenation efforts with the economic upliftment of people dependent on the river.

• Its primary objective is to oversee the implementation of the **Namami Gange Programme**, which focuses on **cleaning and rejuvenating the Ganga River**.
 
• The Council is responsible for strategizing and coordinating efforts for **pollution abatement, river rejuvenation, and ecological sustainability.**
 
 
 
• **Namami Gange Programme:**
 
 
• Launched in **2014**, Namami Gange is a flagship program aimed at **cleaning and rejuvenating the Ganga River**.
 
• It includes projects focused on **sewage treatment, riverfront development, rural sanitation, and afforestation**.
 
• The program emphasizes **preventing pollution** and ensuring sustainable development along the Ganga and its tributaries.
 
 
 
• **Key Pillars of Arth Ganga:**
 
 
• **Zero Discharge:** Promoting zero discharge of untreated waste into the river.
 
• **Economic Activities:** Encouraging organic agriculture, fisheries, and local handicrafts to boost income generation.
 
• **Tourism:** Developing eco-tourism and cultural tourism along the Ganga banks.
 
• **Public Awareness:** Enhancing public awareness and participation in river conservation.
 
 
 
• **Other River-Based Initiatives in India:**
 
 
• **Atal Bhujal Yojana:** Aimed at sustainable groundwater management.
 
• **National River Conservation Plan:** Focuses on improving water quality and reducing pollution in Indian rivers.
 
• **Clean Ganga Fund:** Established to attract contributions for Ganga rejuvenation projects.

questions.question: Banks included in the ______ Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934 are called 'Scheduled Commercial Banks'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Second**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Banks included in the **Second Schedule** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, 1934** are referred to as **Scheduled Commercial Banks**.
 
• A bank is classified under the Second Schedule if it fulfills certain criteria, such as maintaining an average daily balance of a specified amount with the RBI and adherence to specific regulations under the RBI Act.
 
• Scheduled Commercial Banks are eligible for borrowing from the RBI and are entitled to certain privileges, including access to the **RBI's liquidity adjustment facility (LAF)**.
 
• Examples of Scheduled Commercial Banks include major public sector banks, private sector banks, foreign banks operating in India, and Regional Rural Banks (RRBs).
 
• The classification of banks into Scheduled and Non-Scheduled categories ensures proper regulation, financial stability, and monetary control in the banking system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934:**

 
 
• The RBI Act, 1934, provides the framework for the establishment, operations, and regulations of the **Reserve Bank of India**, which acts as the central bank of the country.
 
• The Second Schedule of this Act lists banks that comply with specific statutory conditions, allowing them to be classified as Scheduled Banks.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in ensuring the financial stability of these banks and the Indian economy through its monetary policies.
 
 
 
• **Criteria for Inclusion in the Second Schedule:**
 
 
• A bank must have a minimum paid-up capital and reserves of at least **Rs. 5 lakh**.
 
• The bank's operations should not harm the interests of depositors, and it must comply with the RBI's regulations.
 
• Satisfactory financial stability and operational performance are also key considerations for inclusion in the list.
 
 
 
• **Types of Scheduled Banks in India:**
 
 
• **Public Sector Banks:** Banks where the government holds a majority stake, such as the State Bank of India and Punjab National Bank.
 
• **Private Sector Banks:** Banks like ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank, which are managed by private entities.
 
• **Foreign Banks:** These banks operate in India with headquarters located in other countries, such as CitiBank and HSBC.
 
• **Regional Rural Banks (RRBs):** These banks cater to rural areas and are jointly owned by the Government of India, state governments, and sponsoring public sector banks.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Being a Scheduled Bank:**
 
 
• Access to the **RBI's financial support** and liquidity adjustment facilities.
 
• Participation in the clearinghouse operations conducted by the RBI.
 
• Greater trust among the public due to the regulatory oversight of the RBI.
 
• Eligibility to raise funds at lower interest rates, improving financial stability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Non-Scheduled Banks:**

 
 
• Banks not included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934, are known as Non-Scheduled Banks.
 
• These banks do not meet the statutory criteria specified by the RBI, such as maintaining minimum reserves or being financially stable.
 
• Non-Scheduled Banks are not eligible to borrow funds from the RBI or participate in its liquidity adjustment facilities.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background:**
 
 
• The concept of Scheduled Banks was introduced with the establishment of the RBI in 1935 under the provisions of the RBI Act, 1934.
 
• The classification aimed to streamline the functioning of banks and ensure financial security in the banking sector.
